newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt says Israel gas supply plans still intact.
newsitem.headline: Egypt says Israel gas supply plans still intact.

text.p: Egypt's oil minister said on Monday Egyptian-Israeli differences on the Middle East peace process would not derail long-term plans to supply Israel with natural gas.

Oil Minister Hamdi el-Banbi said technical talks on the proposed deal were continuing, adding that he hoped Israel's peace talks with its Arab neighbours would have progressed by the time the two sides clinched the supply agreement.
"We are not putting politics in front. Egypt is at peace with Israel," Banbi told Reuters at a petroleum conference in the Egyptian capital.
He said a draft agreement was being prepared in Egypt, while Israel has an international company to study gas pipeline routes and establish a master plan for gas utilisation in Israel.

The natural gas deal under discussion anticipates Israel buying two billion cubic metres of gas annually from the year 2000. It would involve building a pipeline from gas fields in Egypt's Delta region to Israel.

The two states have been at peace since 1979 but their traditionally cool ties worsened after Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu took office in May and rejected the handover of occupied Arab lands in exchange for peace.

Egypt's President Hosni Mubarak said he would not meet Netanyahu unless Israel honoured an agreement to withdraw troops from most of the West Bank town of Hebron under a peace deal with the Palestinians.

Banbi had invited Israeli National Infrastructure Minister Ariel Sharon to Egypt for energy talks, but an Israeli spokesman said this month no date would be set until the atmosphere improved between the two countries.

"In our area of energy we have not decided to exchange visits yet," Banbi said when asked whether a new visit had been arranged. "We are delaying such a discussion until the technical staff in both countries finalise things."
Banbi told Reuters in July that the prices Israel offered and the amount of gas it sought could not justify the pipeline costs.
He said on Monday he expected price to remain an issue as the gas belongs to foreign companies, namely Italy's Agip and American firm Amoco.
Tony Barrett, Vice President Middle East for Amoco Natural Gas, said he saw the supply deal as economically-viable but added that it would take time to be realised.
"Probably Egyptian gas is still the most economical source of gas for Israel, Gaza and Jordan. The underlying economics are very good in this transaction," he told Reuters.
